description: The General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT) is NASA's open-source system for space mission design, optimisation and navigation, which NASA describes as the only enterprise, multi-mission open-source tool of its kind. It is developed by a team of NASA, private industry, public and private contributors and has been distributed on SourceForge since 2007. GMAT models spacecraft trajectories in flight regimes from low Earth orbit to lunar, libration point and deep space missions, and is used for real mission operations, engineering analysis, education and outreach. Inputs are spacecraft, force model, propagator and manoeuvre definitions in GMAT scripts or the graphical interface; outputs are propagated trajectories, reports, plots and optimised mission designs. The latest release on SourceForge is R2026a, with release notes in the User's Guide; earlier releases such as R2018a are catalogued in the NASA Software Catalog as GSC-18094-1. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS and is openly accessible online as a free download under the Apache 2.0 licence. Coverage is global and beyond, for any Earth or interplanetary orbit. Caveats: it is a design and analysis tool, not an operational conjunction service, and scenario setup takes expertise. It supports trajectory and coverage studies of satellite infrastructure and its exposure to the space environment; related records are Orekit, Space-Track SATCAT and SPENVIS.
